activity_context.topic_title: Moments and Centers of Mass of Thin Rods

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Mass of a Thin Rod
examples.problem:
The thin rod below has the mass density function $\lambda(x) =2x\, \textrm{kg/m},$ where $x$ is measured in meters. What is the total mass of the rod?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040800/assets/8c8386ff979b46cd994f1ace60f681a6590856e6960e7d74c71a29bb3f0f2d1a.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Given a thin rod oriented along the  $x$-axis over the interval $a \leq x \leq b,$ if $\lambda(x)$ denotes the mass density function of the rod, then the total mass of the rod is given by      

$$
m = \int_a^b \lambda(x) \: \textrm{d}x.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
\lambda(x) = 2x, \qquad 
a=1, \qquad 
b=3.
$$

We calculate the mass of the rod as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =[{x}^{2}]_{1}^{3} \\  & ={3}^{2}-{1}^{2} \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mass of the rod is $8\,\textrm{kg}.$
